target: Round-19 route "m6-walk": the flip graph of realised one-player orientations (mw:flip, mw:tie-edge, mw:cells, mw:monotone, mw:drive-return, mw:b2-return, mw:twelve-flat, mw:no-twelve, mw:h13, mw:w3)

findings.defect: The fence-count bound is false for the class of drive lines the route's own definition admits. def:mw-line lets a drive line have coordinates that are arbitrary rational functions of t without poles on [0,1]; the proof of (a) silently assumes them AFFINE ("det(I-P_sigma(t)) is a polynomial of degree at most m", and "g is a polynomial of degree at most m+1 over that determinant"). For a non-affine drive line the numerator degree is d(m+1), not m+1, and the stated ceiling (m+1)m2^{m-1} fails.
findings.evidence: Counterexample rebuilt in exact arithmetic (audit dir, B/): m=1, delta=1/4. At m=1 the reduced condition p^{0,a}_0=0 forces p=0, so x_sigma=q^{0,sigma}. Take q^{0,0}(t)=1/2 and q^{0,1}(t)=1/2+(t-1/4)(t-1/2)(t-3/4); this is a polynomial (hence pole-free rational) map into Sigma_{1,1/4} (values checked to lie in [0.406,0.594] subset [0,3/4] on a 21-point grid, exact). The two gaps are +/- that cubic, neither identically zero, so the line has 3 fences (t=1/4,1/2,3/4) against the claimed ceiling (m+1)m2^{m-1}=2. Raising the degree of one q breaks the bound at every m. REPAIR: one word -- restrict def:mw-line (or mw:cells(a)) to AFFINE drive lines, or state the bound as d(m+1)m2^{m-1} for coordinate degree d. The finiteness assertion of (a), clauses (b) and (c), and all of mw:monotone, mw:drive-return, mw:b2-return, mw:no-twelve, mw:h13, mw:w3 are unaffected: every application in the route uses affine lines.

findings.defect: The first entry of the printed list of thirteen reversed edges is mislabelled: "(4,beta_1)" should be "(4,alpha_1)". It is the edge {4,6}, whose direction is the same coordinate that entries 8, 10 and 13 of the same list call alpha_1 ((0,alpha_1)={0,2}, (1,alpha_1)={1,3}, (5,alpha_1)={5,7}).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from B2_small_GAME.json in exact arithmetic (B/b2drive.py, own code). Cell 1 = (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2), cell 2 = (0,1,3,6,5,4,7,2); they differ at positions 4 and 6 only, 4 XOR 6 = 2, so the reversed edge is {4,6} in direction bit 1. Direction bit 2 (value 4) is beta_1, fixed by the route's own statement that cell 9 = B^1(.+e_{beta_1}) (indeed cell9 = (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6) = B^1(sigma XOR 4)) and by the double reversal of {3,7} in direction bit 2 at fences 2 and 9. No conclusion changes: with the correct labelling the thirteen reversed edges are still pairwise distinct except {3,7} in beta_1, which occurs twice.

findings.defect: The directed cycle exhibited in the counterexample is not a cycle of t. The route writes "t=(0,5,3,2,6,1,4,7) is a cyclic unique sink orientation containing the directed cycle 1->5->7->3->1"; in t the edge between 5 and 7 points 7->5, not 5->7.
findings.evidence: t[5]=1=001b, so the only out-direction of vertex 5 is bit 0 (5->4); t[7]=7=111b, so all three edges leave 7. Checked in exact combinatorics (B/uso.py): arcs (1,5),(7,3),(3,1) are present, (5,7) is not. The actual cycle of t is 1->5->4->6->2->3->1. The claim that t is a cyclic USO, and everything else in mw:flip(c), is correct: t is a USO and is not acyclic, and the criterion s(1) XOR s(5) = 1 XOR 5 = 4 = e_2 holds.

findings.defect: The reported fence counts cannot be reproduced from the statements: the drive lines are not specified. "Twelve q-lines" on the five-state system with fences 41,35,62,59,59,55,31,35,58,30,49,45, "six one-row lines" with 6,5,5,16,12,28, and "six q-lines" on the six-state witness with 83,106,149,107,83,117 give neither the endpoints of the segments nor which rows move, and a five-state system has ten rows and a six-state one twelve, so the counts twelve and six are not per-row either.
findings.evidence: I re-tested the theorem instead on freshly generated lines out of the H13 system in exact arithmetic (B/lines.py, B/rowline2.py). Six q-lines: gaps affine (second differences vanish at five sample points), 75, 75, 121, 135, 94, 124 fences, all simple, every step a single-edge reversal meeting mw:flip(a), no edge reversed twice, fence count = |Delta(s(0),s(1))| in every case, every cell an AUSO. Three one-row lines (rows 9, 7, 2): the Moebius property confirmed by the vanishing of the 4x4 determinant of (1,t,g,tg) at four points for all 384 incidences, fences located exactly by cross-ratio and verified by substitution: 19, 8, 47, all simple, single-edge, no edge twice, = |Delta|. So mw:monotone holds; only the route's particular numbers are unauditable.

findings.defect: def:mw-graph asserts R_m is "equivalently, by thm:readout-realise, [the set of outmaps] of dyadic delta-leaky readout systems of order (m,1)". thm:readout-realise itself says its two halves "do not close to a size-faithful equivalence" and that the replacement of a rational readout system by a dyadic leaking one "was shown by the route for one player only, by perturbation". The equivalence therefore does hold at r=1, but the citation should point at that clause rather than at the theorem.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex, statement of thm:readout-realise (the paragraph after (b)). Not a defect in the mathematics: at r=1 the one-player perturbation argument is exactly what mw:cells(a) re-runs to place a cell outmap in R_m.

verdict: Everything load-bearing reproduces. I rebuilt, from the statements and not from the route's code, in exact rational arithmetic and in my own C: (1) mw:flip exhaustively over all 12 USOs of the 2-cube (48 reversals) and all 744 of the 3-cube (8928 reversals) -- 0 criterion mismatches, 0 failures of the transposition and path clauses, exactly 48 acyclic-to-cyclic reversals, the printed first example reproduced -- and then over 279552 reversals of 8736 AUSOs of the 4-cube (0 mismatches); the proof of (a) (both directions, via the Szabo-Welzl condition and the 2-face argument), of (b) and of (c) is correct as written. (2) mw:twelve-flat: my own walk-then-complete search returns exactly 480 AUSOs of the 5-cube with a walk of length 12 from 0 and 0 at length 13 (h*(5)=12 independently reproduced), all 480 of height 12 and none Holt-Klee by my own unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test (itself validated against prop:hkfive's height-11 witness and against the 48 height-7 orientations of the 4-cube); my own (F1)-(F4) enumerator returns lem:seven-flat verbatim at m=4 and, at m=5, exactly 240 of the 480, each with a unique admissible partition whose only nontrivial block is the start edge {0,e_x}, x uniform (48 each). (3) mw:no-twelve: the argument reconstructs cleanly against lem:flat-class(c), thm:flat-resolution, cor:ceiling-general, cor:one-tie, lem:tie-perturb and prop:hkfive -- both branches of the dichotomy hand cor:one-tie at most one flat incidence, and the headline h*_1(5)=h*_1^nd(5)=h*_LP(5)=h*_HK(5)=11 follows (the lower bound from prop:hstar-one-eleven's witness, which I also re-verified from its game). (4) mw:h13: the 418-vertex game verifies from the file -- one player, out-degree two, greatest trap EMPTY hence stopping, average part acyclic, first-passage rows equal to the printed table at denominator 2^14, p_vv=0 and least leak 5/16384, 64 exact 6x6 solves, outmap as printed with no tied incidence and least margin exactly 226793593012712537793143/3187971438880543888553754624, USO, acyclic, Holt-Klee, height 13 attained at 25,27,57,59, the printed run and switched sets, every one of the 13 rounds productive with the value vector monotone, longest run over all 64 starts 13; the consequences via prop:oneplayer-plus-one (h*_1(7)>=14, h*_LP(7)>=14, h*_1(m)>=m+7, h*_1(8)>=15 superseding prop:hstar-one-eight) and cor:stack-family (h*_1(7k-1)>=13k, liminf >= 13/7 > 11/6) check against the actual text of those labels, and rem:hk-survey does record h*_1(6)>=13 as open. (5) mw:b2-return: recomputed from B2_small_GAME.json -- normal form reproduced from the game, 14 cells, the 13 rationals of rem:pinned-escape confirmed exactly as the fences, all 14 cell outmaps matching the route's table, all Holt-Klee of the stated heights, every transition a single-edge reversal meeting mw:flip(a), the edge {3,7} in beta_1 reversed twice, and |Delta(cell1,cell14)| = 11, which is also the true flip distance in F_3 and in W_3 (BFS). (6) mw:w3: 728 acyclic, 656 Holt-Klee, both flip graphs connected, W_3 of min degree 3, max degree 12, average degree 5.415, heights 1..4. ONE DEFECT SURVIVES, and it is a mis-scoped hypothesis rather than a wrong computation: mw:cells(a)'s fence bound (m+1)m2^{m-1} is proved only for AFFINE drive lines while def:mw-line admits arbitrary pole-free rational ones, and I give an explicit rational (indeed polynomial) drive line at m=1 with 3 fences against the ceiling 2. That is why sound is false; the repair is one word, and nothing else in the route rests on it -- mw:monotone, which is what every application uses, is stated for affine lines and I re-verified its full content (gaps affine or Moebius, every fence simple, single-edge reversals, no edge reversed twice, fence count exactly |Delta|) on six fresh q-lines and three fresh one-row lines built from the H13 system. The remaining findings are a mislabelled coordinate in one printed edge, a wrong directed cycle in one illustrative parenthetical, and two unreproducible measurement blocks in verification fields.
